name: Hive
description: Insect chess, surround your opponent's Queen Bee
rules:
Two players take turns placing or moving insect pieces on a hex board. Completely surround the opponent's Queen Bee (all 6 neighbor spaces filled) to win.

Placement:
- On your turn, place a new piece from your reserve OR move a piece already on the board.
- New pieces must touch one of your own and never touch an opponent's piece (except the very first placement).
- Your Queen Bee must be placed by your 4th turn.

Piece movement:
1. Queen Bee — slides 1 adjacent space.
2. Beetle — moves 1 adjacent space; may climb on top of other pieces and stack (the top piece defines that stack's color).
3. Spider — slides exactly 3 empty spaces around the hive (no backtracking).
4. Ant — slides any number of empty spaces around the hive.
5. Grasshopper — jumps in a straight line over one or more contiguous pieces, landing on the first empty space beyond them.

One-Hive rule: the hive must stay a single connected group at every moment, including mid-move — a piece that would split the hive cannot be moved.

No-Gate rule: a sliding piece cannot squeeze through a 1-space gap flanked by pieces on both sides (Grasshoppers and Beetles are unaffected).

log.gameDraw: both queens surrounded — it's a draw!
